fatal_errors: The proposed grain-size mechanism does not reconstruct the target temperature-driven transition from dislocation/stacking-fault deformation to lattice disorder above approximately 900 K.
No prior evidence is cited despite the request to identify supporting evidence.
Annealing at 900 °C is asserted to refine grains from 10 μm to 1 μm without specifying a grain-refining process; ordinary annealing would more commonly promote recovery and grain growth.
The predicted 25–30% changes and the 20% falsification threshold are unsupported and arbitrary.
The test does not isolate grain size because annealing can also alter segregation, residual stress, phase constitution, oxidation behavior, and coating–substrate adhesion.
explanation: The response addresses wear and microscopic deformation and supplies an explicit baseline, parameter range, comparative experiment, and falsification rule. However, it replaces the target intervention and mechanism with an unsupported grain-size hypothesis. It omits the Cu substrate geometry, nanoscale coating, 300–1200 K temperature series, indentation/friction protocol, and the key approximately 900 K boundary. It also fails to predict the observed sharp loss of hardness and wear resistance, elastic-modulus maximum near 600 K, increasing friction, or correlations among HCP fraction, dislocation density, and lattice disorder. The alternative could be tested in principle, but its processing premise is questionable, its experiment is confounded, and it has no evidentiary support.
